mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 rally over the next 60 trading days as capital goods lag behind housing activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), indicates a broad-based supply shock that elevates input costs and reduces profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98 AND RSAFS < previous 3-month average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for two months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which historically precedes a compression in earnings growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which historically precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending rises.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 3.5% for two consecutive months with concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 99 signals a synchronized labor and supply downturn, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 3.5% for two consecutive months AND INDPRO < 99
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous six-month average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery that typically precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as construction-related equities outperform.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 95% confidence.
